"Explain the Question:Compare s/p character in N–H and P–H bonds
Concept:Hybridisation, Bent’s rule, bond parameters
Solution:

• Molecules shown are NH3 and PH3
• In NH3, nitrogen is sp3 hybridised, so lone pair and N–H bonds have mixed s and p character
• In PH3, phosphorus uses almost pure p orbitals for P–H bonding due to poor s–p mixing
• Hence, P–H bonds have higher p-character than N–H bonds
• Lone pair on N has more s-character than lone pair on P
• Therefore, %p in P–H bond (X8) is greater than %p in N lone pair (X2)

Final Answer:Option-3"
